_comment: The KlickTipp-only parts of a stored editor document. The editor itself does not know them:
they are added by KlickTipp, live next to 'page' (decisions and AI blocks) or inside a module
(add-ons), and they are the parts an HTML round trip cannot preserve.
Both top-level keys are removed before the document is rendered to HTML. So they are not in the
HTML anyone edits, and a full content replacement DELETES them -- not degrades them. Announce
that before replacing; nothing an editing agent does can preserve them.
Conditional content. The definitions sit in this top-level array; the *place* they apply to is
marked inside the content with HTML comments carrying the same id:
<!--DECISION_START(42)--> … <!--DECISION_END(42)-->.
Markers without their definition are meaningless, which is the second reason a round trip
loses conditional content even when the markers survive.
Consumers walk decision.segments[].conditions[] and read 'type' plus 'entity' to find out
which tag, product or other entity a newsletter depends on.

conditions.type: the condition option, e.g. an entity class name
conditions.condition: the chosen condition of that option

notes.entity: 0 when the chosen condition needs no entity; otherwise the id of the referenced entity.
notes.conditionsOpAND: true = all conditions of the segment are AND-joined, false = OR.
notes.segmentsOpAND: true = all segments are AND-joined, false = OR.
notes.emptyIsNormal: An empty array means the newsletter has no conditional content.

_comment: Blocks whose text is generated per recipient. The array holds the instructions, one entry per
block; the rendered result is what a round trip brings back, so the instruction is lost and
the text stops being generated.

shape.name: name given by the user
fieldIds: ids of the contact fields the instruction may use

notes.fieldIds: Strings. Empty when the instruction uses no contact field.
notes.tagIds: Integers. Empty when the instruction is not restricted by tags.
notes.malformed: A non-empty value that is not a list of objects is broken data, not an empty state.

_comment: KlickTipp add-ons are ordinary modules of the single 'addon' kind -- countdown, contact card,
Wowing video, AI text, personalized email and signature are indistinguishable by type. The
concrete add-on is named in 'moduleInternal.uid' -- a sibling of 'descriptor', NOT inside it,
and 'moduleInternal.configurationUi.contentDialogId' repeats the same handle. An earlier
version of this file put it under 'descriptor.contentDialog.id', which matches nothing in a
real document; the path below was read off stored newsletters. A rule written against the
type matches all add-ons or none.
A round trip brings back the rendered output; the add-on itself is gone.
Which add-ons an account is even offered is decided when the editor is configured, not by
the document. Read off the client's own editor configuration:
- AI text appears only with the 'smart-copy-writer-access' flag; without it the add-on is
filtered out of the editor configuration entirely.
- The personalized email is switched off unless the email is used in an automation: the
entry stays in the configuration but is not offered for insertion, so blocks already in a
newsletter keep working while no new one can be added there by a person. Newsletters
carrying one exist and are legitimate; leave them alone.
An add-on inserted past those rules sits in a newsletter the account cannot open, configure
or switch off -- so a tool that writes documents has to honour them itself.
A stored add-on module also carries 'entity', 'placeholder', 'ctaLabel' and a base64 'icon'
inside 'moduleInternal'. Those are a snapshot: the editor is handed label, call-to-action
and placeholder from KlickTipp's own configuration on every load, translated per account
language -- and one stored newsletter was found carrying resolved German text while another
carried the untranslated keys. So they say nothing about the add-on and must not be copied
into a new block: doing so freezes one account's language into another's newsletter.
What identifies an add-on is 'uid' plus 'configurationUi.contentDialogId'. Nothing else.

customerFacingTerms._comment: What to call these things in anything a person reads. Never the keys or handles.
customerFacingTerms.addon: add-on, named by its handle above
